question: A calculates his profit percentage on the selling price of an article, whereas B calculates his profit on the cost price of the same article. The selling price of both of them is the same and both get 40% profit. If the difference between their profits is Rs. 120, then the selling price (in Rs.) of the article is:
solution:
Given:

The selling price of both of them is the same and both get 40% profit. 

The difference between their profits is Rs. 120.

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + Profit%)

Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Calculation:

Let the seling price of the article for both A and B be Q.

Cost price for A = Q - Q × 40%

⇒ 0.6Q

Profit of A = Q - 0.6Q

⇒ 0.4Q = 4Q/10

Cost price of B = Q ÷ (1 + 40%)

⇒ Q/(1 + 0.4)

⇒ Q/1.4

⇒ 5Q/7

Profit of B = Q - 5Q/7

⇒ 2Q/7

According to the question,

4Q/10 - 2Q/7 = 120

⇒ (28Q - 20Q)/70 = 120

⇒ 8Q = 120 × 70

⇒ Q = 8400/8

⇒ Q = 1050

∴ The selling price of the article is Rs. 1,050.
